source.original_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure and H a complete real inner-product normed space. Let F:E→H have actual ambient Frechet derivative D(w):E→H for every w. Assume nonnegative M1,M2, an operator bound norm(D(w))<=M1 on the closed unit ball and an operator-Lipschitz bound norm(D(w)-D(u))<=M2 norm(w-u) there. Fix y in H. On the actual unit-norm subtype S define K(w)=F(w), angular cost c(u,v)=arccos(inner(u,v)), the actual Bochner mean m(mu)=integral K dmu, V_mu(w)=2 inner(m(mu)-y,F(w)), and G_mu(w)=2P_w D(w)^*(m(mu)-y) with the explicit projection P_w z=z−⟨z,w⟩w, which projects onto w-perpendicular when norm(w)=1. Let Q(mu,nu) be the literal extended nonnegative infimum of the quadratic angular cost over all actual couplings. There exist C1,C2>0, independent of probability laws and unit weights, such that for every actual parameter probability K is integrable, V_mu has the displayed ambient gradient 2D(w)^*(m(mu)-y) at every ambient w, and its projected G_mu is tangent and uniformly bounded by C1 at every unit weight. For every two actual parameter probabilities Q is finite and norm(G_mu(w)-G_nu(u))<=C2*(sqrt(Q).toReal+c(w,u)). Feature boundedness, strong measurability, feature Lipschitz control and residual budgets are derived inside the proof rather than assumed; the returned conclusions are feature integrability, actual ambient gradient, tangency/uniform bound, finite transport cost and the joint sensitivity estimate. The constants may depend on the displayed feature/derivative data, E,H and y. This is a generic feature-law theorem, not a concrete Gaussian scalar-data potential, installed manifold-gradient/Wasserstein API or intrinsic path-length theorem.

theorem result
    {E H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H]
    (F : E → H) (D : E → E →L[ℝ] H)
    (hF : ∀ w, HasFDerivAt F (D w) w)
    (M₁ M₂ : ℝ) (hM₁ : 0 ≤ M₁) (hM₂ : 0 ≤ M₂)
    (hBound : ∀ w : E, ‖w‖ ≤ 1 → ‖D w‖ ≤ M₁)
    (hLip : ∀ w u : E, ‖w‖ ≤ 1 → ‖u‖ ≤ 1 → ‖D w-D u‖ ≤ M₂*‖w-u‖)
    (y : H) :
    let S := {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1}
    let K : S → H := fun w => F w.1
    let c : S × S → ℝ := fun z => Real.arccos ⟪z.1.1,z.2.1⟫_ℝ
    let m : Measure S → H := fun μ => ∫ w, K w ∂μ
    let V : Measure S → E → ℝ := fun μ w => 2 * ⟪m μ-y,F w⟫_ℝ
    let G : Measure S → E → E := fun μ w =>
      (2 : ℝ) • ((D w).adjoint (m μ-y) - ⟪(D w).adjoint (m μ-y),w⟫_ℝ • w)
    let Q : Measure S → Measure S → ℝ≥0∞ := fun μ ν =>
      AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.Transport.transportCost
        (fun z => ENNReal.ofReal ((c z)^2)) μ ν
    ∃ C₁ C₂ : ℝ, 0 < C₁ ∧ 0 < C₂ ∧
      (∀ μ : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure μ →
        Integrable K μ ∧
        (∀ w : E, HasGradientAt (V μ) ((2 : ℝ) • (D w).adjoint (m μ-y)) w) ∧
        ∀ w : S, ⟪w.1,G μ w.1⟫_ℝ = 0 ∧ ‖G μ w.1‖ ≤ C₁) ∧
      ∀ μ ν : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure μ → IsProbabilityMeasure ν →
        Q μ ν ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ w u : S,
          ‖G μ w.1-G ν u.1‖ ≤
            C₂ * ((Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal + c (w,u))

blind_reconstruction.text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space E equipped with its Borel measurable structure, every complete real inner-product normed space H, every map F:E->H and assignment D:E->(E->L[R]H), assume F has full ambient Frechet derivative D(w) at every w:E. Let M1,M2 be supplied nonnegative real numbers, with norm_op(D(w))<=M1 for every norm_E(w)<=1, and norm_op(D(w)-D(u))<=M2*norm_E(w-u) for every w,u in the closed unit ball. Fix any y:H. Use the following literal definitions. Let S={w:E | norm_E(w)=1}, with its inherited topology and measurable structure, and write w_bar for the ambient representative of w:S. Set K(w)=F(w_bar) and c(w,u)=arccos(inner_product_E(w_bar,u_bar)). For every measure mu on S define m(mu)=integral_S K(w) dmu(w) in H. For mu:Measure S and ambient w:E set V(mu,w)=2*inner_product_H(m(mu)-y,F(w)), and G(mu,w)=2 times ((D(w)).adjoint(m(mu)-y)-inner_product_E((D(w)).adjoint(m(mu)-y),w) times w). Define Q(mu,nu) as the infimum in the nonnegative extended reals of integral_lower_{S times S} ofReal(c(w,u)^2) dgamma(w,u), over all actual product-space measures gamma whose first pushforward marginal is mu and second is nu. Here integral_lower is the nonnegative extended Lebesgue integral. The empty feasible infimum is infinity, and no optimizer is selected or asserted. The map ofReal takes the nonnegative part, and the vector mean is the actual Bochner integral, totalized to zero if it is not genuinely integrable. Then all the following hold: There exist real C1>0 and C2>0, fixed for all the following laws and points. For every probability mu on S, K is genuinely Bochner integrable under mu; for every ambient w:E, V(mu,.) has gradient 2 times (D(w)).adjoint(m(mu)-y) at w; and for every unit-subtype point w:S, inner_product_E(w_bar,G(mu,w_bar))=0 and norm_E(G(mu,w_bar))<=C1. For every probability pair mu,nu on S, Q(mu,nu)!=infinity and for every w,u:S, norm_E(G(mu,w_bar)-G(nu,u_bar))<=C2*((Q(mu,nu)^(1/2)).toReal+c(w,u)). HasGradientAt means that the full real Frechet derivative in any direction v is inner_product_E(2 times (D(w)).adjoint(m(mu)-y),v)=2*inner_product_H(m(mu)-y,D(w)(v)). Mu is fixed when taking that derivative, and the ambient point w is not restricted to the unit ball in this gradient conclusion. For norm_E(w)=1, G(mu,w) is the orthogonal projection of this ambient gradient onto the subspace perpendicular to w. It is that projected vector which receives the uniform norm and transport-plus-angle estimates; the statement does not substitute G for the full ambient gradient. The means are defined for arbitrary laws by the totalized integral formula, but the stated integrability and estimates are conditional on the laws being probabilities. No feature integrability or finiteness of Q is supplied as a hypothesis: those are conclusions. Q is the actual squared-angular-cost infimum. Its explicit finiteness makes its extended square root finite, so toReal is the ordinary nonnegative real value and not its special value zero at infinity. No positive lower bound on Q is assumed. The final estimate compares two arbitrary probability laws and two exact unit points with the same C2; it is not restricted to finite support. The constants may depend on the fixed E,H,F,D,M1,M2,y but not on mu,nu,w,u. They are strictly positive without an asserted formula or sharpness, while the supplied M1,M2 are only nonnegative. No positive-dimensionality or nonempty-unit-set premise appears; if S is empty the probability-conditioned clauses are vacuous, while the existence of positive C1,C2 is still asserted. The concrete angular cost and infimum definitions do not assert a new metric/geodesic API or an attained optimal coupling, and no derivative with respect to the law variable is stated.

theorem quadratic_feature_law_gradient_angular_transport_control
    {E H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H]
    (F : E → H) (D : E → E →L[ℝ] H)
    (hF : ∀ w, HasFDerivAt F (D w) w)
    (M₁ M₂ : ℝ) (hM₁ : 0 ≤ M₁) (hM₂ : 0 ≤ M₂)
    (hBound : ∀ w : E, ‖w‖ ≤ 1 → ‖D w‖ ≤ M₁)
    (hLip : ∀ w u : E, ‖w‖ ≤ 1 → ‖u‖ ≤ 1 → ‖D w-D u‖ ≤ M₂*‖w-u‖)
    (y : H) :
    let S := {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1}
    let K : S → H := fun w => F w.1
    let c : S × S → ℝ := fun z => Real.arccos ⟪z.1.1,z.2.1⟫_ℝ
    let m : Measure S → H := fun μ => ∫ w, K w ∂μ
    let V : Measure S → E → ℝ := fun μ w => 2 * ⟪m μ-y,F w⟫_ℝ
    let G : Measure S → E → E := fun μ w =>
      (2 : ℝ) • ((D w).adjoint (m μ-y) - ⟪(D w).adjoint (m μ-y),w⟫_ℝ • w)
    let Q : Measure S → Measure S → ℝ≥0∞ := fun μ ν =>
      AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.Transport.transportCost
        (fun z => ENNReal.ofReal ((c z)^2)) μ ν
    ∃ C₁ C₂ : ℝ, 0 < C₁ ∧ 0 < C₂ ∧
      (∀ μ : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure μ →
        Integrable K μ ∧
        (∀ w : E, HasGradientAt (V μ) ((2 : ℝ) • (D w).adjoint (m μ-y)) w) ∧
        ∀ w : S, ⟪w.1,G μ w.1⟫_ℝ = 0 ∧ ‖G μ w.1‖ ≤ C₁) ∧
      ∀ μ ν : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure μ → IsProbabilityMeasure ν →
        Q μ ν ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ w u : S,
          ‖G μ w.1-G ν u.1‖ ≤
            C₂ * ((Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal + c (w,u)) := by
  let : SecondCountableTopology E := inferInstance
  let S := {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1}
  let K : S → H := fun w => F w.1
  let c : S × S → ℝ := fun z => Real.arccos ⟪z.1.1,z.2.1⟫_ℝ
  let m : Measure S → H := fun μ => ∫ w, K w ∂μ
  let V : Measure S → E → ℝ := fun μ w => 2 * ⟪m μ-y,F w⟫_ℝ
  let G : Measure S → E → E := fun μ w =>
    (2 : ℝ) • ((D w).adjoint (m μ-y) - ⟪(D w).adjoint (m μ-y),w⟫_ℝ • w)
  let Q : Measure S → Measure S → ℝ≥0∞ := fun μ ν =>
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.Transport.transportCost
      (fun z => ENNReal.ofReal ((c z)^2)) μ ν
  change ∃ C₁ C₂ : ℝ, 0 < C₁ ∧ 0 < C₂ ∧
    (∀ μ : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure μ →
      Integrable K μ ∧
      (∀ w : E, HasGradientAt (V μ) ((2 : ℝ) • (D w).adjoint (m μ-y)) w) ∧
      ∀ w : S, ⟪w.1,G μ w.1⟫_ℝ = 0 ∧ ‖G μ w.1‖ ≤ C₁) ∧
    ∀ μ ν : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure μ → IsProbabilityMeasure ν →
      Q μ ν ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ w u : S,
        ‖G μ w.1-G ν u.1‖ ≤ C₂ * ((Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal + c (w,u))
  have hFc : Continuous F := continuous_iff_continuousAt.mpr fun w => (hF w).continuousAt
  have hKsm : StronglyMeasurable K := (hFc.comp continuous_subtype_val).stronglyMeasurable
  have hChord (w u : E) (hw : ‖w‖ ≤ 1) (hu : ‖u‖ ≤ 1) :
      ‖F w-F u‖ ≤ M₁*‖w-u‖ := by
    apply (convex_closedBall (0 : E) 1).norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasFDerivWithin_le
      (fun z _ => (hF z).hasFDerivWithinAt) ?_
      (by simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right] using hu)
      (by simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right] using hw)
    intro z hz
    exact hBound z (by simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right] using hz)
  let B := ‖F (0:E)‖+M₁+1
  have hB : 0 ≤ B := by dsimp [B]; positivity
  have hKb (w : S) : ‖K w‖ ≤ B := by
    have hb := hChord w.1 0 w.property.le (by simp)
    have hn := norm_add_le (F w.1-F 0) (F 0)
    rw [sub_add_cancel] at hn
    simp only [sub_zero,w.property,mul_one] at hb
    change ‖F w.1‖ ≤ B
    dsimp [B]
    linarith
  have hAng := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.UnitSphereAngularCost.unit_sphere_angular_cost_properties (E := E)
  change Continuous c ∧ Measurable c ∧
    (∀ u v : S, 0 ≤ c (u,v) ∧ c (u,v) ≤ Real.pi ∧
      c (u,v) = InnerProductGeometry.angle u.1 v.1 ∧ ‖u.1-v.1‖ ≤ c (u,v) ∧
      (c (u,v) = 0 ↔ u = v) ∧ c (u,v) = c (v,u)) ∧
    ∀ u v w : S, c (u,w) ≤ c (u,v)+c (v,w) at hAng
  have hc0 (z : S × S) : 0 ≤ c z := (hAng.2.2.1 z.1 z.2).1
  have hcB (z : S × S) : c z ≤ Real.pi := (hAng.2.2.1 z.1 z.2).2.1
  have hKlip (w u : S) : ‖K w-K u‖ ≤ M₁*c (w,u) :=
    (hChord w.1 u.1 w.property.le u.property.le).trans
      (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hAng.2.2.1 w u).2.2.2.1 hM₁)
  have hMean (μ ν : Measure S) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [IsProbabilityMeasure ν] :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.BochnerMeanTransport.bounded_bochner_mean_quadratic_transport_control
      K hKsm B Real.pi M₁ hB Real.pi_pos.le hM₁ hKb c hAng.2.1 hc0 hcB hKlip μ ν
  have hTangent :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.QuadraticFeatureTangentGradient.quadratic_feature_potential_tangent_gradient
      F D hF M₁ M₂ hM₁ hM₂ hBound hLip
  let R₀ := B+‖y‖
  have hR₀ : 0 ≤ R₀ := add_nonneg hB (norm_nonneg y)
  have hResidual (μ : Measure S) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] : ‖m μ-y‖ ≤ R₀ :=
    ((hMean μ μ).2.2.2.2 y).1
  have hGrad (μ : Measure S) (w : E) :
      HasGradientAt (V μ) ((2 : ℝ) • (D w).adjoint (m μ-y)) w := by
    rw [hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt]
    have he : InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E ((2 : ℝ) • (D w).adjoint (m μ-y)) =
        (2 : ℝ) • innerSL ℝ ((D w).adjoint (m μ-y)) := by
      ext v
      simp [InnerProductSpace.toDual_apply_apply,innerSL_apply_apply]
    rw [he]
    exact hTangent.1 (m μ-y) w
  let A := 2*M₁^2
  let B₂ := 2*(M₂+2*M₁)*R₀
  have hA : 0 ≤ A := by dsimp [A]; positivity
  have hB₂ : 0 ≤ B₂ := by dsimp [B₂]; positivity
  refine ⟨2*M₁*R₀+1,A+B₂+1,by positivity,by positivity,?_,?_⟩
  · intro μ hμ
    let : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := hμ
    refine ⟨(hMean μ μ).1,hGrad μ,?_⟩
    intro w
    have ht := hTangent.2.1 (m μ-y) w.1 w.property
    refine ⟨ht.1,?_⟩
    exact ht.2.2.trans ((mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hResidual μ) (by positivity)).trans (by linarith))
  · intro μ ν hμ hν
    let : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := hμ
    let : IsProbabilityMeasure ν := hν
    refine ⟨(hMean μ ν).2.2.1,?_⟩
    intro w u
    have hm : ‖(m μ-y)-(m ν-y)‖ ≤ M₁*(Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal := by
      simpa only [sub_sub_sub_cancel_right] using (hMean μ ν).2.2.2.1
    have hr := hResidual ν
    have ht := hTangent.2.2 (m μ-y) (m ν-y) w.1 u.1 w.property u.property
    have hpoint := (hAng.2.2.1 w u).2.2.2.1
    have ht' : ‖G μ w.1-G ν u.1‖ ≤
        A*(Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal+B₂*c (w,u) := by
      calc
        _ ≤ 2*M₁*‖(m μ-y)-(m ν-y)‖+
            2*(M₂+2*M₁)*‖m ν-y‖*‖w.1-u.1‖ := ht
        _ ≤ 2*M₁*(M₁*(Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal)+
            2*(M₂+2*M₁)*R₀*c (w,u) := by
          gcongr
        _ = _ := by dsimp [A,B₂]; ring
    apply ht'.trans
    have hs : 0 ≤ (Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal := ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
    have hc := hc0 (w,u)
    nlinarith [mul_nonneg hA hc,mul_nonneg hB₂ hs]

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.QuadraticFeatureLawGradient

steps.text: Differentiability gives continuity. The convex mean-value bound on the closed unit ball produces the M1 chord Lipschitz estimate. Continuity on a second-countable domain yields strong measurability of the feature restriction even when H is not separable.

steps.title: Produce one uniform feature bound
steps.text: Compare every unit feature with F(0), using the previous estimate and the norm triangle inequality. The extra one makes B a convenient positive budget. This budget is an internal consequence, not a new premise.
steps.lean:
let B := ‖F (0:E)‖+M₁+1

steps.title: Pass from chords to angular cost
steps.text: The canonical angular-geometry result supplies measurability, nonnegativity, the pi upper bound and chord domination. Consequently K is M1 Lipschitz with respect to the actual angular cost.

have hAng := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.UnitSphereAngularCost.unit_sphere_angular_cost_properties (E := E)
  change Continuous c ∧ Measurable c ∧
    (∀ u v : S, 0 ≤ c (u,v) ∧ c (u,v) ≤ Real.pi ∧
      c (u,v) = InnerProductGeometry.angle u.1 v.1 ∧ ‖u.1-v.1‖ ≤ c (u,v) ∧
      (c (u,v) = 0 ↔ u = v) ∧ c (u,v) = c (v,u)) ∧
    ∀ u v w : S, c (u,w) ≤ c (u,v)+c (v,w) at hAng
  have hc0 (z : S × S) : 0 ≤ c z := (hAng.2.2.1 z.1 z.2).1
  have hcB (z : S × S) : c z ≤ Real.pi := (hAng.2.2.1 z.1 z.2).2.1
  have hKlip (w u : S) : ‖K w-K u‖ ≤ M₁*c (w,u) :=
    (hChord w.1 u.1 w.property.le u.property.le).trans

steps.text: Apply bounded Bochner transport to actual probability laws, not chosen optimal couplings. It produces integrability, finite Q, the mean difference estimate and the residual budget R0=B+norm(y).

  have hTangent :=

steps.text: Projection contraction gives the pointwise bound, while R0 is independent of the parameter law. Choose strictly positive C1,C2 before quantifying over all laws and weights. The constants are not claimed dimension free.

let A := 2*M₁^2

steps.title: Combine law and point movement
steps.text: Use the tangent-field joint estimate, substitute the actual mean sensitivity and residual budget, and dominate the chord by the angle. All costs are finite before applying toReal; the sum of the two coefficients plus one yields a single constant.

· intro μ ν hμ hν
    let : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := hμ
    let : IsProbabilityMeasure ν := hν

    intro w u
    have hm : ‖(m μ-y)-(m ν-y)‖ ≤ M₁*(Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal := by
      simpa only [sub_sub_sub_cancel_right] using (hMean μ ν).2.2.2.1

    have ht := hTangent.2.2 (m μ-y) (m ν-y) w.1 u.1 w.property u.property
    have hpoint := (hAng.2.2.1 w u).2.2.2.1
    have ht' : ‖G μ w.1-G ν u.1‖ ≤
        A*(Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal+B₂*c (w,u) := by
      calc
        _ ≤ 2*M₁*‖(m μ-y)-(m ν-y)‖+

          gcongr
        _ = _ := by dsimp [A,B₂]; ring
    apply ht'.trans
    have hs : 0 ≤ (Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal := ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
    have hc := hc0 (w,u)
    nlinarith [mul_nonneg hA hc,mul_nonneg hB₂ hs]

lesson.lean_statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure and H a complete real inner-product normed space. Let F:E→H have actual ambient Frechet derivative D(w):E→H for every w. Assume nonnegative M1,M2, an operator bound norm(D(w))<=M1 on the closed unit ball and an operator-Lipschitz bound norm(D(w)-D(u))<=M2 norm(w-u) there. Fix y in H. On the actual unit-norm subtype S define K(w)=F(w), angular cost c(u,v)=arccos(inner(u,v)), the actual Bochner mean m(mu)=integral K dmu, V_mu(w)=2 inner(m(mu)-y,F(w)), and G_mu(w)=2P_w D(w)^*(m(mu)-y) with the explicit projection P_w z=z−⟨z,w⟩w, which projects onto w-perpendicular when norm(w)=1. Let Q(mu,nu) be the literal extended nonnegative infimum of the quadratic angular cost over all actual couplings. There exist C1,C2>0, independent of probability laws and unit weights, such that for every actual parameter probability K is integrable, V_mu has the displayed ambient gradient 2D(w)^*(m(mu)-y) at every ambient w, and its projected G_mu is tangent and uniformly bounded by C1 at every unit weight. For every two actual parameter probabilities Q is finite and norm(G_mu(w)-G_nu(u))<=C2*(sqrt(Q).toReal+c(w,u)). Feature boundedness, strong measurability, feature Lipschitz control and residual budgets are derived inside the proof rather than assumed; the returned conclusions are feature integrability, actual ambient gradient, tangency/uniform bound, finite transport cost and the joint sensitivity estimate. The constants may depend on the displayed feature/derivative data, E,H and y. This is a generic feature-law theorem, not a concrete Gaussian scalar-data potential, installed manifold-gradient/Wasserstein API or intrinsic path-length theorem.
